clips.send: Tarim Basin. About 1000 m (3,300 ft). China’s largest basin, between the Tianshan and Kunlun Mountains. The Taklimakan, China’s largest desert, fills its centre. The Tarim River is China’s longest inland river; rich in oil and gas (start of the West–East Gas Pipeline). Tarim equals biggest basin + biggest desert.

clips.send: What if a whole country were built like a giant staircase? China is: high in the west, low in the east, dropping in three great steps from the Tibetan Plateau (青藏高原 Qīng–Zàng Gāoyuán, the “Roof of the World”, higher than almost every mountain top in the lower 48 states) down to the sea. Spin the 3D model, switch on the step colours, and drag the cross-section to walk down the stairs.

clips.send: Tibetan (Qinghai–Tibet) Plateau. Average over 4000 m (13,000 ft). The highest plateau in the world: the “Roof of the World”. Snow-capped ranges and glaciers everywhere; “mountains from afar, flat valleys up close”. It forms the first step. Source of the Yangtze and the Yellow River. Four plateaus in one word each: Tibetan HIGH, Inner Mongolian FLAT, Loess BROKEN, Yunnan–Guizhou RUGGED.

clips.send: Inner Mongolian Plateau. About 1000 m (3,300 ft). China’s second-largest plateau, on the second step. Wide, flat and open: “you can see to the horizon”. Huge grasslands such as Hulunbuir and Xilin Gol. FLAT: “The sky is vast, the land boundless; the wind bends the grass and you see the cattle and sheep.”

clips.send: A plateau (高原 gāoyuán) is high but fairly flat on top, like the Colorado Plateau. A basin (盆地 péndì) is a low bowl ringed by mountains, like the Great Basin in Nevada. A plain (平原 píngyuán) is low and flat, like the Great Plains. Hills (丘陵 qiūlíng) are low and gently rolling. Mountains (山地 shāndì) are high and steep, like the Rockies.

clips.send: Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau. 1000–2000 m (3,300–6,600 ft). Rugged land with many small flat basins called “bazi” (坝子). Karst (limestone) landforms are widespread, e.g. the Stone Forest. On the second step; its eastern edge is the Xuefeng Mountains. RUGGED: “No three li of flat land.”

clips.send: Middle–Lower Yangtze Plain. Mostly below 50 m (160 ft). Low and flat, with many rivers and lakes and a dense water network. Called the “land of fish and rice” (鱼米之乡). Includes the Lianghu, Poyang Lake and Yangtze Delta plains. Yangtze Plain equals rivers + lakes + fish + rice.

clips.send: Loess Plateau. 1000–2000 m (3,300–6,600 ft). The world’s largest area of loess, thick yellow soil. Cut into countless gullies: “a thousand ravines and ten thousand gullies”. Serious soil erosion feeds mud into the Yellow River. BROKEN: thousands of gullies. Bounded by Taihang (E), Wushaoling (W), the Great Wall (N), Qinling (S).

clips.send: 黄土高原。 海拔 1000—2000 米。 世界上黄土分布面积最广的高原，黄土层深厚。 地表千沟万壑，支离破碎。 水土流失严重，大量泥沙进入黄河。 “碎”：千沟万壑。东到太行山，西到乌鞘岭，北到长城，南到秦岭。

clips.send: 塔里木盆地。 海拔约 1000 米。 我国面积最大的盆地，位于天山与昆仑山之间。 盆地中部是我国最大的沙漠——塔克拉玛干沙漠。 塔里木河是我国最长的内流河；石油、天然气丰富（西气东输的起点）。 塔里木：最大的盆地 + 最大的沙漠。

clips.send: 青藏高原。 平均海拔 4000 米以上。 世界上海拔最高的高原，被称为“世界屋脊”。 雪山连绵，冰川广布，“远看是山，近看成川”。 构成我国地势的第一级阶梯，是长江、黄河的发源地。 四大高原一字诀：青藏“高”、内蒙古“平”、黄土“碎”、云贵“崎”。

clips.send: 长江中下游平原。 海拔大多在 50 米以下。 地势低平，河湖众多，水网密布。 被誉为“鱼米之乡”。 包括两湖平原、鄱阳湖平原、长江三角洲等。 长江中下游平原：河湖多，鱼米乡。

clips.send: 山脉的走向。 山脉构成了地形的“骨架”。 东西走向：北列天山、阴山，中列昆仑山、秦岭，南列南岭。 东北、西南走向：西列大兴安岭、太行山、巫山、雪峰山，中列长白山、武夷山，东列台湾山脉。 西北、东南走向：阿尔泰山、祁连山；南北走向：贺兰山、横断山脉；弧形：喜马拉雅山脉。 山区（山地、丘陵和比较崎岖的高原）约占全国面积的 3分之2。
clips.text: 山脉的走向。 山脉构成了地形的“骨架”。 东西走向：北列天山—阴山，中列昆仑山—秦岭，南列南岭。。 东北—西南走向：西列大兴安岭—太行山—巫山—雪峰山，中列长白山—武夷山，东列台湾山脉。。 西北—东南走向：阿尔泰山、祁连山；南北走向：贺兰山、横断山脉；弧形：喜马拉雅山脉。。 山区（山地、丘陵和比较崎岖的高原）约占全国面积的 2/3。
